message.content:
Yes—if you’re experiencing excessive or disruptive noise in Atlanta, you can file a complaint with the city’s authorities. Here’s how you can do it: | Step | What to Do | Where to Go | |------|------------|-------------| | **1. Identify the source** | Determine whether the noise is coming from a residential, commercial, or public property. | — | | **2. Check the noise ordinance** | Atlanta’s Noise Ordinance (Title 10, Chapter 5 of the Atlanta Municipal Code) sets limits on allowable decibel levels and defines “noisy” activities. It also lists prohibited times (e.g., 11 p.m.–7 a.m.) and special rules for construction, events, and businesses. | [Atlanta Municipal Code – Title 10](https://www.atlantaga.gov/municipal-code) | | **3. Gather evidence** | Take note of the date, time, duration, and nature of the noise. If possible, record audio or video (but be mindful of privacy laws). | — | | **4. File a complaint** | • **Phone:** Call 311 (or 911 if it’s an emergency).
• **Online:** Use the City of Atlanta’s “Report a Problem” portal.
• **In person:** Visit the City Hall or the local police precinct. | • 311: 404‑555‑1234 (replace with actual number)
• Online portal: https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 | | **5. Follow up** | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. You can track the status via the portal or by calling 311. | — | ### Quick Tips - **Timing matters:** If the noise occurs during restricted hours (usually 11 p.m.–7 a.m.), it’s more likely to be actionable. - **Construction & Events:** These have special permits; check if the activity has a valid permit before filing. - **Noise from neighbors:** If it’s a recurring issue, consider talking to your neighbor first—sometimes a friendly reminder resolves the problem. If you’re unsure whether the noise violates the ordinance, you can also consult the City of Atlanta’s *Noise Control* page or contact the *Department of Public Safety* for guidance.
